c0d7e971a4349deb.label: MAKE
c0d7e971a4349deb.summary: Journal of Environmental Psychology study (82 adults, 1,189 paired nights): bedroom heat disrupts restorative deep sleep and drops next-day focus. Hook: 'Can't focus at work? Check the temperature in your bedroom last night.'
c0d7e971a4349deb.notes:
- Study published in the Journal of Environmental Psychology (Eric W. Dolan, Nov 2026).
- Sample: 82 working adults in Austria, 1,189 paired sleep-and-work days tracked via room air monitors, wearable sleep rings (Oura), and smartwatch check-ins.
- Findings: night-to-night heat increases caused fragmented rest, reduced slow-wave restorative sleep, and directly degraded self-reported executive focus and work recovery the following day.
- Practical takeaway: cooling bedroom environment by 1-2 degrees C yields compounding cognitive benefits for knowledge workers.
